name: Millikelvin torsion-balance de Haas-van Alphen and Hall/SdH magnetotransport of HOPG graphite, 30 mK-3.8 K, up to 12 T
plain_name: Detect quantum oscillations in graphite's magnetism near absolute zero
description: Measure the de Haas-van Alphen effect of a 10 x 5.5 x 0.5 mm HOPG piece with a capacitive torsion-balance magnetometer, then Hall and Shubnikov-de Haas resistance on the same sample (six-terminal Hall bar, AC currents below 10 uA), in the mixing chamber of a low-vibration dilution refrigerator from 30 mK to 3.8 K in a superconducting magnet up to 12 T.
keywords: Detect quantum oscillations in graphite's magnetism near absolute zero

sources.citation: S.B. Hubbard, T.J. Kershaw, A. Usher, A.K. Savchenko, A. Shytov, 'Millikelvin de Haas-van Alphen and Magnetotransport studies of Graphite', arXiv:1007.2573 (2010)

requirements.rationale: The lowest measurement temperature (30 mK, where all FFT and phase analyses were done) must be reachable at the sample.
Cyclotron masses come from the temperature dependence of the oscillation amplitude over 30 mK-3.8 K (data at 30, 485, 980 and 3830 mK).
The magnetization and transport sweeps extend to 12 T.
Hall and SdH resistance were measured on the sample in six-terminal geometry, so wired sample contacts are needed (the torsion balance is also read out electrically as a capacitance).
Optional detail: the six-terminal Hall bar needs at least six sample leads.
The 10 mm x 5.5 mm HOPG footprint has a circumscribed diameter of 11.42 mm (sqrt(10^2+5.5^2) = 11.413 mm, rounded up), which the sample space must clear.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
